crossfire-premier.summary: Crossfire Premier (Redmond) runs ECNL and ECNL Regional League teams from U13, with a Pre-ECNL/Academy layer at U11–U12 and year-round RCL 'Premier' teams from U9; below that sits the separate Crossfire Select programme, whose teams are lettered A/B/C and frequently named after their coach (e.g. 'Crossfire Select BU15 A (Chatta)'), and a Crossfire Jr / U8 Spring RCL intake for the youngest. ECNL sides carry two-year bands in their names ('B13/14 ECNL 1') while the club's own charts list single birth years, so both forms are the same club. The coaches page lists staff without team assignments; the Select naming is where a coach's surname becomes part of a team name, which matters when two Select sides differ only by that surname — they are two teams.

coaches.name: Tim Reynolds
coaches.role: Girls ECNL Director; Player & Coach Development

coaches.name: Claire Knock
coaches.role: DOC Girls U13–U19 ECNL RL/RCL; Leadership Academy Coordinator

eastside-fc.summary: Eastside FC states its ladder outright: at U13–U19 the ECNL team is top and ECNL RL second, both based in Preston, then Red, White, and Blue/Grey/Navy grouped by level; at U8–U12 Red and White are the top two, with Pre-ECNL I and II at U11–U12 as the feeder to the ECNL pathway. 'West' teams (Red/White in Bellevue, Maroon on Mercer Island) are separate training hubs whose level varies by age — a West team may sit alongside Blue or Grey. Colours therefore rank teams here. Ages are single-year (U-labels on an Aug 1–Jul 31 window). Every coach's team assignments are published, so a team name plus a coach's name identifies a side.

coaches.name: John Yorke
coaches.role: Director of Coaching; Boys ECNL Technical Director

coaches.name: Scott Ford
coaches.role: Coach; Tournament Director (NW Summer Showcase Olders)

washington-premier-fc.summary: Washington Premier FC (Puyallup) fields ECNL teams — the club calls them its Black/ECNL teams and says they travel the most — and RCL teams named by colour, Black above White (its FAQ cites a 'G09 White' side winning RCL Division 3 and moving up). Ages are single birth years (G09). The recreational side is a separate programme, Washington United, for ages 4–14. The staff-coaches page lists names and start years but no team assignments, so a coach name does not identify a team here.

seattle-united.summary: Seattle United publishes a team-by-team coach list for every age group. At U13–U19 the ECNL team is top and ECNL RL second; below them the Premier (RCL) teams are named Copa, Tango, Samba and Nova in that order of standing, with Pre-ECNL at U11–U12 sitting above Copa. Regional (NPSL 'Regional Select') teams carry a hub prefix — Shoreline, Northwest or South — and within a hub Blue is first, White second, Black third. The site labels teams by birth year ('B13 ECNL') while ages are two-year seasonal bands (Aug 1–Jul 31), so 'B13/14 ECNL' in a league listing is the same side. Because a coach's teams are published, a coach name plus age group identifies the tier — useful when a fixture list drops the squad word.

pacnw-sc.summary: PacNW SC (Starfire, Tukwila) lists every coach with their teams, and each team name carries its league in brackets: ECNL and ECNL-RL at U13–U19, Pre-ECNL at U11–U12, then RCL teams named Maroon, Blue, White and Gold, and NPSL teams named Gold, Silver and Copper. The girls staff table orders ECNL, ECNL-RL, Maroon (RCL), Blue (RCL) top to bottom, and the boys table orders White (RCL), Gold (RCL), then Gold/Silver/Copper (NPSL), so colours are a ladder here — but note Gold appears in both the RCL and NPSL lists, so the bracketed league is what separates 'BU10 Gold (RCL)' from 'BU8 Gold (NPSL)'. Ages are single seasonal-year groups (Aug 1–Jul 31). Pac Federal Way and Southlake are volunteer-run select/rec affiliates under the same club.

coaches.name: Brandon Mitalas
coaches.role: Director of Soccer / Director of Coaching

sound-football-club.summary: Sound FC (Woodinville) is the RCL charter club for South Snohomish County and Northshore. Its boys U13–U19 first teams play MLS NEXT 2 from 2025–26 and its girls U13–U19 first teams join Girls Academy Aspire for 2026–27; below those sit RCL premier teams and a Juniors programme at U8–U10. The site names directors and a few coaches without team assignments and gives no squad-colour scheme, so two Sound FC teams in one age group cannot be told apart from the website — the league is the only tier signal.

highline-premier-fc.summary: Highline Premier FC forms several teams per age group and places each in a league by readiness — RCL or WPL, and from Fall 2026 Elite Academy for selected 11v11 boys teams. The site publishes no team names, squad colours or coach-to-team assignments, only its leadership team, so the league a team plays in is the only public tier signal.

north-kitsap-soccer-club.summary: North Kitsap Soccer Club (Poulsbo) is a volunteer-coached club with one competitive tier, 'Select', playing in the Washington Premier League, plus Pre-Comp and Rec. Its teams are known by nicknames rather than colours — Lady Berserkers, Serpents, Sound Vipers, Valkyries and so on — and where an age group has two teams the nickname is the only thing that separates them (Girls 2010/2011 Lady Berserkers vs Serpents; Boys 2013 Sound Vipers vs Avalanche); the site gives no order between them. Ages appear as birth years, sometimes two-year ('2010/2011'). From 2026–27 a joint U19 girls team is run with Bainbridge Island FC and Sequim FC.

valor-soccer.summary: Valor Soccer (Southeast King County) has three competitive tiers by name — Elite, Premier, Select — plus Rec. Elite is the national-league layer (boys MLS NEXT / ECNL-RL from 2026–27, girls GA Aspire), Premier plays RCL with teams named Gold, Black and Grey in that order, and Select plays NPSL. Pre-ECNL at U11–U12 is offered to the top Premier teams and plays RCL Division 1. Coaches are listed by tier (Premier coaches, Select coaches) but not by team, so a coach name gives the tier, not the team.

whatcom-fc-rangers.summary: Whatcom FC Rangers (Bellingham) publishes every 2026/27 team with its coach. At U13 and up the first team is ECNL RL and the second is Blue (Silver third where it exists); at U9–U12 the ladder is Gold, Blue, Silver, with Gold sometimes absent (Boys U12 has only Blue and Silver, so Blue is the first team there). Colours therefore rank teams, but the top colour varies by age group. Ages are single seasonal years; social posts still use birth years ('2009 Gold'). Girls U16/U17 Blue is one combined team.

western-washington-surf.summary: Western Washington Surf runs two programmes, Elite and Premier, each split into lettered teams: Elite A teams play the EA League (boys) or DPL (girls) from U11 and NPL for older boys; Elite B teams play WPL; Premier A teams play WPL and Premier B and C teams sit below. Elite is split North (Bellevue/Redmond) and South (Puyallup/Tacoma); Premier is organised by training hub (Tacoma, Medina, Redmond, Puyallup, Yelm). So 'Surf Tacoma B' encodes hub and letter, and Elite vs Premier is the first cut. The staff page lists 37 coaches without team assignments, and the /teams page shows Inland Surf (Spokane) sides, so coach names do not place a Western WA Surf team.

coaches.name: Christa Hinchcliffe
coaches.role: Team Coach U10; Assistant Coach U14

west-sound-soccer-academy.summary: West Sound Soccer Academy is a girls-only, women-led club on Bainbridge Island with one team per age group from U9 to U19 (a combined U16–19 side), all playing in the Washington Premier League. There are no tiers or squad colours to resolve; each age group has a named team coach. Ages follow the Aug 1–Jul 31 seasonal year from 2026–27.

bvb-international-academy-washington.summary: BVB International Academy Washington (Borussia Dortmund's affiliate) selects the top players in each age group for its Elite Academy (EA) teams, branded 'BVB IA Washington'; the Eastside (Bellevue) and Seattle locations then form 2nd and 3rd teams that play NPL and WPL. So the location word in a team name is the tier: 'Washington' = EA first team, 'Eastside' or 'Seattle' = second/third team in NPL or WPL. Ages follow the Aug 1–Jul 31 seasonal year from 2026–27. The tryout page names EA age-group coaches for U12–U15 only; the coaching staff page was not captured.

coaches.name: Matthew Olson
coaches.role: Interim Head Coach; Director of Coaching

eagleclaw-fc.summary: Eagleclaw FC (Starfire, Tukwila) is 'powered by' Valencia CF; the top tier is the affiliated Valencia CF Academy Seattle, whose 'VCF' teams play Elite Academy (boys) or WPL (girls), while Eagleclaw's own 'EFC' teams — at most an A and a B per birth year — play WPL. The staff page assigns coaches by team with the VCF/EFC prefix, so a coach name places a team in the ladder.

coaches.name: George Bundy
coaches.role: Assistant Director of Coaching; Youth Director

kitsap-alliance-fc.summary: Kitsap Alliance FC (Bremerton) names its first team in every age group Blue and its second White; from U13 the Blue team carries an 'N1' prefix because it plays the National 1 League, and BU12 Blue is a Pre-ECNL side for 2026–27. The rest play RCL. The team list gives a coach for most teams, so a coach name identifies Blue or White. Ages are single seasonal years.

coaches.name: Luke Howells
coaches.role: Director of Coaching; Director of Tournaments

mt-rainier-fc.summary: Mt. Rainier FC (Buckley) labels its competitive teams Academy-1, Academy-2, Red and White, in that order: Academy is the top programme and Premier (Red, White) the one below, with Jr. Academy-1/2 as the 7v7 sides at U8–U10. The 2026/27 coaching allocation names a coach for every team by age group, so a coach plus age group gives the tier — e.g. Boys U13 Academy-1 is Tyler Williams, Boys U13 Red is Jimmy Mwenyeheri. Ages are single seasonal years. A fixture name like 'Mt. Rainier FC B14/15 Academy' is an Academy-1 or -2 side, distinct from that age group's Red.

seattle-reign-academy.summary: Seattle Reign Academy is girls-only. At U13–U19 the first team plays the Girls Academy league and the second plays GA Aspire, so the league is the tier. At U8–U12 (Pre-Academy) there are two or three teams per age group in the WPL, named Gold and Navy, with the Gold and Navy U11/U12 sides moving to GA Inspire for 2026–27. The 2026/27 coaching slate is a separate page that was not captured; only the technical staff are named here.

northwest-united-fc.summary: Northwest United FC (Skagit County) fields ECNL-RL first teams for boys and girls with RCL and NPSL teams beneath them; its site menu groups teams exactly that way. No squad colours or team-level coach assignments are published — the staff page is a name list — so the league is the only public tier signal. Ages move to the Aug 1–Jul 31 seasonal year for 2026–27.

mukilteo-youth-soccer-club.summary: Mukilteo Youth Soccer Club runs Recreational, Select and Premier programmes, with the competitive teams playing in the Washington Premier League (and NSRL) under the name Mukilteo FC; an Instagram caption on the home page calls a side 'MYSC FC B', suggesting lettered squads. The site publishes no team list, colour scheme, or coach names — coaches are volunteers who register through GotSport — so nothing on the website separates two Mukilteo teams in one age group.

norpoint-soccer-club.summary: Norpoint Soccer Association (NE Tacoma) is a recreational club with a Select programme; the site is a TeamSnap page with no team list, tiers, colours, or coach names. Nothing here tells two Norpoint teams apart.

rayados-soccer-academy-northwest.summary: Rayados Soccer Academy Northwest is CF Monterrey's affiliate; its competitive 'Academy' teams (U10–U15) play NPL and WPL, with a Junior Academy and Mini-Stripes below. No team names, squad markers, or coach-to-team assignments are published; six staff are named.

south-kitsap-soccer-club.summary: South Kitsap Soccer Club (Port Orchard) is a recreational club whose premier programme plays as 'SK United'. So a team named SK United is this club's competitive side. No team list, colours, or coaches are published; rec ages are counted as of July 31.

dragons-fc.summary: Dragons FC is a Tukwila non-profit whose competitive teams play the WPL Super and Classic leagues; the rec programme feeds them (its page even says it prepares players 'for top Crossfire Premier teams'). No team names, colours, or coaches are published.

cascade-fc.summary: Cascade FC is the premier club of the Snoqualmie Valley Youth Soccer Association and plays in the RCL. The site names three directors and no teams, colours or team coaches.

sozo-fc.summary: Sozo FC (Yakima Valley) names teams Gold, Royal and White. The premier-teams page pairs each with its league: the boys U13–U19 Gold teams play MLS NEXT while the Royal team in the same age group plays RCL, and at U9–U12 Gold plays RCL where Royal plays WPL — so Gold is the first team, Royal second, White third. Older age groups are written as two-year bands ('Boys 2007/08 Gold'). Every team has a named head coach, and several coaches take a Gold and a Royal side in different age groups, so the coach plus age group identifies the tier.

washington-rush.summary: Washington Rush lists its 2026–27 premier teams per age group in a fixed order that is the ladder: for boys MLSN (MLS NEXT) or Pre MLSN first, then Rush, Nero, Azul, Cinza; for girls GA (Girls Academy) or Pre-GA first, then Rush, Nero. A boys U18/19 'NL' team plays National League beside the MLSN side. So 'Rush' in a team name is a tier word (the top non-national team), not just the club name, and the Italian/Portuguese colours rank the rest. Every team has a named coach. Ages are single seasonal years.

atletico-futbol-club.summary: Atlético Fútbol Club is a Seattle access-focused club whose Instagram bio reads 'MLS NEXT | Elite Academy', so its top teams play those two national leagues. Only the home page was captured; no team names, colours or coaches.

blackhills-fc.summary: Blackhills FC's site is an OTTO Sport app shell; the only captured text is a footer with the RCL logo. Tiers, colours and coaches are unknown from the website.

emerald-city-fc.summary: Emerald City FC publishes its 2026–27 teams as a grid whose columns are, left to right, EA, Green, White, Blue, Black — that is the ladder. Boys U13–U19 first teams play Elite Academy; below that and at younger ages the colours rank Green > White > Blue > Black (girls have Green, White, Blue only; GU15/16 is a combined White side). Each cell names the coach, so a coach plus age group gives the tier: BU12 Green is Kerry Hamel, BU12 Black is Clyde Wight.

everett-youth-soccer-club.summary: Everett Youth Soccer Club plays as 'Everett FC' (its Instagram handle is everett_fc_eysc) and, per a club directory, runs Premier, Select and Rec programmes with a Fuerza FC affiliation; the website itself renders only its title to any reader, so tiers, colours and coaches are unknown. Do not confuse it with Everett Soccer Club in Massachusetts.

harbor-soccer-club.summary: Harbor Soccer Club (Gig Harbor) has Elite Academy teams for boys and Girls Academy Aspire teams for girls above its Harbor Premier programme, which the Player Pathway page splits into age phases rather than tiers. The coaching staff page is empty ('Add Content...'), and no team colours are published, so nothing on the site separates two Harbor Premier teams in one age group.

lake-washington-premier-fc.summary: Lake Washington Premier FC names every team 'White' plus a fish — B2014 White Sharks, B2014 White Piranhas, B2014 White Mantas are three teams in one birth year — so here the colour means nothing and the fish name is the squad marker. Teams play the WPL at Super, Classic or Copa level. Every team has a named head coach, and the club says two coaches stay with a team from U9 to U19, so a coach name is a durable key for a LWPFC team. Ages are single birth years.

northlake-soccer-club.summary: Northlake Soccer Club is a small premier club founded in 2016; only the home page was captured, which names the two founders and no teams.

northshore-select-club.summary: Northshore Select Club is the NPSL select programme of the Northshore Youth Soccer Association — a middle tier by design, with Sound FC as the association's premier club above it. No team names or coaches are published.

pilchuck-soccer-alliance.summary: Pilchuck Soccer Alliance's competitive programme is 'Force Select', so teams named Force or PSA Force are this club. No team list or coaches on the captured page.

pumas-seattle.summary: Pumas Seattle is a Pumas UNAM-affiliated soccer school for low-income youth with seven age categories; nothing on the captured home page names teams or coaches.

seattle-celtic.summary: Seattle Celtic states its 2026–27 ladder plainly: top boys teams (2008–2013 age groups) in MLS NEXT, top girls in the Girls Academy, second boys teams in Elite Academy, and every other league team in the WPL. The league is therefore the tier. Ages are the new two-year bands ('2013/14'). Thirty-five head coaches are listed by name with no team assignments.

sparta-tacoma.summary: Sparta Tacoma is North Tacoma Soccer Club's premier programme. Its highest boys teams are the 'Red' teams and play the Elite Academy league from U11; the rest play WPL. Ages are given as birth year with U-label ('2015/U11', '2007-2008/U18/19'). No coach names on the captured page.

united-sports-fc.summary: United Sports FC is a multi-location club (Bellevue, Redmond, Bothell, Sammamish, plus California and New York) whose Washington competitive teams play the WPL. Teams are likely told apart by location and colour (a 'United Sports FC B14/15 Navy' appears in fixtures) but the site publishes no team list or coaches.

warriors.summary: Warriors Sports Academy (Bellevue, 'Little Warriors') has two tiers: 'EA' teams in the Elite Academy league are the first teams (boys U11–U18), and 'Attack' teams play WPL (girls U15 Attack in DPL/WPL). At U9–U10 there are two Attack teams, Blue and Gold, with no stated order. The 2026/27 team table names a coach per team. Ages are single seasonal years.

washington-east-surf-soccer-club.summary: Washington East Surf SC is the Inland Northwest Surf umbrella with regional branches (Spokane, Palouse, Columbia Basin, Blue Mountain, River Valley, Canyon Range); it fields Girls Academy teams and, in Columbia Basin, Elite Academy teams, with Surf Select below. Only the home page menu was captured.

wenatchee-fa.summary: Wenatchee FA names its boys teams by two-year band and colour, listed top-down as ECNL-RL Black, Red, White, Grey — so Black is the first team (carrying 'ECNL-RL' at U13–U19), Red second, White third, Grey fourth. The programme page maps leagues to tiers: ECNL-RL for the top boys teams, RCL / RCL-N1 below, WPL Classic/Copa for the rest, PAL at U10–U12. Every boys team has a named head coach and often an assistant; the girls page was not captured.

snohomish-united.summary: Snohomish United's real website is snohomishunited.org (the .com in our directory is a parked GoDaddy page). Its staff page lists every head coach with 2025–26 teams, which reveals the ladder: boys first teams are ECNL and girls first teams ECNL-RL (boys ECNL-RL is a second team), and below the national leagues the RCL/NPSL teams are named Black, Red and White — Black appears wherever there is one such team, Red and White where there are more, so Black is the first of them. Ages are single years, sometimes with the birth year in brackets ('GU14 (2012) Black'). The coach list is the way to place a Snohomish side whose name in a fixture list lacks the colour.

stanwood-camano-youth-soccer-club.summary: Stanwood-Camano Youth Soccer Club's competitive teams play as 'Spartan FC', a volunteer-run select programme (U9–U18) that the club describes as a level between Recreational and Premier. So a team named Spartan FC in a fixture list is this club. No team colours or coaches are published; the site refuses automated readers (HTTP 403) and was read in a browser.
